findings.title: Rotation origin contradicts the exact round-trip geometry claim
findings.problem: §7.1 defines (x,y) as the top-left of the unrotated box with rotation about the box center, but §9.4 loads/commits Fabric objects with 'origin top-left' and angle=rotationDeg. In Fabric a top-left origin rotates about the top-left corner, not the center, so the two sections describe incompatible pivots. For any rotated layer, obj.left/top is the rotated anchor, not the §7.1 top-left, so out-of-bounds detection (§9.6), the print-area artwork crop (§8.2/§11.5), and the review bounds flag misplace/mis-crop it, and the 'exact reopen/side-switch' guarantee (criterion 13 requires rotation preservation) is false.
findings.fix: Pick one pivot and make both sections agree. Recommended: use Fabric center origin and store (x,y) as the box center in template units (load left=x*s, top=y*s; commit x=obj.left/s, y=obj.top/s). If (x,y) must remain the unrotated-box top-left, load with center origin and convert left=(x+width/2)*s, top=(y+height/2)*s, converting back on commit. Update §9.6/§11.5 bounds math to compute the rotated AABB from that single definition.

findings.title: Textbox corner-scaling not folded into fontSize/width; text size lost on reload
findings.problem: The schema stores no scaleX/scaleY and commit reads fontSizeUnits=obj.fontSize/s. Fabric Textbox corner handles change scaleX/scaleY, not fontSize, so a corner-scaled text layer commits the pre-scale font size while rendering fontSize*scaleY tall. On reload fontSize=fontSizeUnits*s with scale discarded, so text reloads at the wrong size, breaking exact preservation for text.
findings.fix: Normalize text scale into metrics on commit: on scaling/modified set fontSize=round(obj.fontSize*obj.scaleY), width=obj.width*obj.scaleX, then reset obj.scaleX=obj.scaleY=1 before reading geometry back; or disable corner (uniform-scale) controls for Textbox and allow only side (wrapping width) handles plus the fontSize field. State which in §9.4.

findings.title: Sticker recolor is a named feature with no field in the data model to persist it
findings.problem: §8.5 lists 'recolor-where-the-SVG-allows' for stickers, but stickers serialize as ImageLayer (§7.1), which has no fill/tint/color field. Any applied recolor cannot be serialized and will not survive save/reopen or a side switch; if stickers are flattened to a bitmap blob it is not expressible at all.
findings.fix: Either (a) drop the sticker recolor claim (keep move/resize/rotate/opacity/duplicate/delete/reorder, which the model supports) and update §8.5; or (b) add an optional fill?: string to a sticker-specific layer type with a stated rule (sets fill on the sticker SVG's recolor target, applied at load before rasterizing) and specify stickers are kept as parsed/inline SVG, not a flattened bitmap. Pick one explicitly.

findings.title: Sticker storage uses an unresolved 'X or Y' with a correctness trap
findings.problem: Stickers are 'promoted into IndexedDB on first use (or referenced by a reserved sticker:<id> blobKey scheme).' The two strategies are not equivalent: the IDB-promotion branch stores a bundled sticker's blob only in the user's IndexedDB, so a data-clear / IDB wipe / private-mode fallback (§11.3) turns a first-party sticker into the missing-blob placeholder, contradicting the never-broken-images posture. The reserved sticker:<id> scheme has no such failure.
findings.fix: Commit to the reserved sticker:<id> blobKey scheme: the blob resolver recognizes the sticker: prefix and loads markup from data/stickers.ts / src/assets/stickers directly, never from IndexedDB, so bundled stickers always resolve. Reserve IndexedDB promotion for user-uploaded images only. Remove the 'or'.

findings.title: Export output resolution / sₑ never pinned to a number
findings.problem: §11.5 says 'fixed export scale' and §9.4 references sₑ without a value; only §8.6 mentions '2000px' in passing. The export dimension is not single-sourced or concrete.
findings.fix: State in §11.5: export longest edge = 2000px ⇒ sₑ = 2000 / viewBox.width, as a shared config constant used by both artwork-only and mockup exports.

findings.title: Inlining the same garment SVG many times produces duplicate element ids
findings.problem: Category grid, hero, and showcase inline garment SVGs each carrying id=garment-body (and garment-trim). Duplicate ids in one document are invalid HTML; safe only because queries are ref-scoped and the reference SVG has no url(#id) references. Any future gradient/filter/clipPath url(#id) will cross-wire.
findings.fix: Namespace/uniquify ids on inject (prefix per instance and rewrite internal url(#…) refs), or state the invariant: garment SVGs must contain no internal url(#id) refs and recolor targets are matched by a scoped data-recolor attribute, not a document id.

findings.title: Quantity direct-input validation behavior unspecified
findings.problem: Bounds (1..999) and a Stepper exist, but behavior for typed out-of-range/non-numeric quantity input is unspecified, unlike the thorough rules for upload (§10.1), text (§10.2), and rename (§11.2).
findings.fix: Add to §12: quantity input is clamped to [1,999]; non-numeric/empty reverts to the last valid value on blur; totals recompute from the clamped value.
